absent: Locking and concurrency rules for the blacklist list, initcall tables and boot state transitions are not shown.
Exact binary layout, sizes, alignment and numeric encodings of list, namespace, banner and device number objects are not shown.
Full command line grammar, return code meanings beyond skip on veto and missing file tolerance, and unknown option policy are not shown.
Internals of cross dossier setup helpers invoked during boot and of time, preemption and allocation primitives are not shown.
Failure handling for early allocation, symbol resolution and trace registration beyond warn and continue is not shown.

findings.text: The top level boot routine is globally visible so early platform code can transfer control to it, and it does not return to its caller once handoff to the surviving boot continuation occurs.

Top level bring up runs with interrupts held off through processor, memory, scheduler and timing preparation, then enables interrupts once and completes caching, namespace and accounting preparation before delegating to the later init continuation.

Bring up observes coarse phase order where scheduling becomes usable before timer activity, timekeeping precedes full randomness, early workqueue admission precedes execution, and console output follows late slab readiness, ending in a non returning handoff.

Interrupts remain disabled from entry through early setup, a boot flag records that state, checks warn if enabling happened early and force disabled state again, and a single enable marks the end of the early disabled window.
When ramdisk start lies below the lowest usable page frame the boot path disables the ramdisk and emits a diagnostic, preventing use of overwritten early memory.
Single init routine invoker is visible outside early boot so modular code can reuse the same guarded invocation path.

Guarded invocation first consults the blacklist and skips vetoed targets, then traces start, calls the target, traces completion, and finally validates execution state before returning the target result and mixing additional entropy.

After each init routine the invoker compares preemption depth and interrupt state against entry values, warns on mismatch, restores the entry preemption depth and re enables interrupts when they were left disabled.

Leveled initialization walks eight named stages in fixed order over successive slices of a table bounded by per level markers, reparsing boot arguments for each stage with unknown options ignored, plus a distinct early range before the first named stage. Order is pure, core, postcore, arch, subsys, fs, device, late.

Blacklist input is a comma separated list where each element is copied into separately allocated storage linked onto a global list, and matching normalizes the resolved symbol name by discarding any module suffix at the first space before exact comparison, with diagnostics on listing and on veto.
A build without symbol name support cannot blacklist, so listing requests warn and do nothing while the veto check always allows execution.
Blacklist node holds intrusive list linkage for membership in the global veto list together with a pointer to an owned zero terminated name copy.

Initcall debugging records a timestamp at start and logs caller identity, then at completion logs identity with return value and elapsed microseconds, and logs each entered level name. One build routes through tracepoints registered at debug enable time while the other calls the same logging helpers directly when the debug flag is set.

Basic setup groups symmetric multiprocessing cpuset finalization with driver model, interrupt proc setup, constructor execution and leveled calls, while a separate pre multiprocessing helper executes only the early table range with level tracing labeled early.
Global constructor iteration is omitted entirely on UML where the host runtime already ran them, even though constructor support remains enabled for modules.

Post boot thread first synchronizes outstanding asynchronous boot work and releases and hardens init memory while moving system state toward running, then attempts userspace launch in strict priority and halts if no candidate succeeds.

Userspace launch prefers a ramdisk command when present, then an explicit command whose failure halts, then a configured default whose failure only warns, then four fallbacks where absence is tolerated but presence without executability warns, ending in halt when all fail. Fallback order is sbin init, etc init, bin init and bin shell paths.

Freeable boot preparation enables fuller allocation and secondary processors, runs remaining early and leveled setup with health detection and built in tests, waits for and validates early userspace and root readiness including ramdisk command accessibility and conditional namespace preparation, then loads integrity material.

Read only hardening defaults to enabled, an architecture hook gets first chance to consume its boot option, otherwise on and off values toggle the flag and other values warn, and final marking only enforces strict read only mappings and checks when both the hardening build option and the flag agree.

Early userspace environment creation makes a device directory with mode 0755, a console character node with owner read write mode derived from major 5 minor 1, and a restricted root directory with mode 0700, while console attachment opens the console node and duplicates it onto the first three descriptors, warning when the open fails.
Initial UTS namespace combines common namespace linkage with six name fields for system, node, release, version, machine and domain, anchored to the initial user namespace.

Two human readable version banners are provided, one for boot log identifying release builder host compiler and version, and one format for proc output with release and version placeholders alongside builder host and compiler.
Early hostname handling copies its argument into the node name field with bounded length and warns when truncation occurs.
Level boundaries are held in an ordered table of nine markers delimiting eight stages plus the table end, paired with an ordered table of eight stage names.
Weak placeholder definitions for the initial namespace and boot banner allow a stronger build provided object to take precedence.
Initial namespace and version strings are globally visible for early identity and logging use.
